strings.mealDescription1: Following the guidance of the Anticipatory Action Manual, describe the M&E plan for this EAP. Including:
strings.mealDescription11: EAP Monitoring (between the trigger moment and the implementation of the actions)
strings.mealDescription12: Impact evaluation plan: how, when and by whom will the robust impact evaluation to assess how early actions reduced the humanitarian impact of the extreme event be conducted. Please note that the IFRC DREF...
strings.mealDescription13: Trigger evaluation by whom, when and how the trigger evaluation will be conducted)
strings.mealDescription14: Learning (when, who and how the learning will take place. E.g workshop, interviews etc).
strings.mealDescription2: If a more detailed M&E plan is available add it as an annex.
strings.mealDescription3: Describe how the Anticipatory Action M&E plan is linked to the existing PMER system of the National Society. If the NS does not have a PMER system, explain how the EAP will be used to strengthen this area prior to activation
strings.mealExplanatoryNote: Building evidence about the impact of Anticipatory Action systems is a priority. Therefore, the EAP should include an M&E plan to 1) assess the impact of the early actions and the extreme event after each activation and 2) identify if all activities were carried out as planned and document how early actions were implemented 3) learn from the process to improve the system in the future. The chapters 4.3 Design M&E plan and 6. Activate, Monitor, Evaluate in the Anticipatory Action Manual, provide guidance on the set-up and implementation of the monitoring, evaluation, learning tools. Ideally, the M&E system should be set up to allow comparison of impacts between communities that received early actions and those that didn´t (please refer to Anticipatory Action manual for more information). This M&E plan should be harmonized with the existing IFRC PMER guidance and tools, available on FedNet.
strings.mealAttachRelevantFilesDescription: Attach any additional maps, documentation, files, images, etc.
strings.mealCriteriaIntroduction1: The EAP must include planning and budget for the following:
strings.mealCriteriaIntroduction11: A post-distribution monitoring survey/exercise adapted to Anticipatory Action (see quality criteria for topics to cover and examples)
strings.mealCriteriaIntroduction12: A post-activation lessons learned workshop to document how early actions were implemented, assess the activation process (including whether all activities were carried out as planned), identify lessons learned, and make recommendations for improvements (if applicable). Note that additional days can be added onto the lessons learned workshop in order to make updates directly to the EAP (in advance of resubmission) or if further work is required, to develop a plan for incorporating learning into the EAP and budget.
strings.mealCriteriaIntroduction13: Monitoring and reporting that enables the National Society to report on the proportion of the activation budget successfully spent before the hazard peaked.
strings.mealCriteriaComment1: An intervention-relevant PDM survey (or other exercise) should be developed before the activation so that is it ready for prompt implementation following the activation. Readiness funds may be used to develop the PDM and should be planned and budgeted in year one
strings.mealCriteriaComment2: The PDM should capture themes essential to anticipatory action that are not necessarily captured in normal PDMs, including:
strings.mealCriteriaPdmTheme1: When people first received early warning or the impending hazard, from whom, and via what channel.
strings.mealCriteriaPdmTheme2: What actions, if any, the household took based upon the warning.
strings.mealCriteriaPdmTheme3: When the community/household received each component of the anticipatory assistance (in relation to the hazard onset and/or peak).
strings.mealCriteriaPdmTheme4: Whether or not the aid could be used (as intended) before the hazard peaked, for the following:
strings.mealCriteriaPdmFollowing1: Perceived severity of the event in relation to other events in the last-ten years.
strings.mealCriteriaPdmFollowing2: If anticipatory cash is included, when (i.e. before, during, after the event) and on what any anticipatory cash was spent.
strings.mealCriteriaPdmFollowing3: Satisfaction with the timing of the aid: would it have been more useful if it arrived earlier, later, or was appropriately timed?
strings.mealCriteriaComment3: Monitoring should also reflect on the transition from early action to early response.
strings.mealCriteriaComment4: In addition, National Societies should consider including a trigger model review as part of the lessons learned exercise (particularly in case of non or partial activation).
strings.mealCriteriaComment5: National Societies should review the RCRC Anticipatory Action Manual, Chapter 9: Prepare Activation Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning for more guidance on MEAL approaches for anticipatory action.
